ATTACHMENT A: THE 11 UNKNOWN LACKS AND OPERATIONAL GAPS IN CAPSTONE 1

During real-world development and testing under Capstone 2, the team discovered eleven (11) critical engineering omissions in the Capstone 1 documentation where theoretical assumptions broke down under live operational constraints:
Identified Hidden Gap / Omission in Capstone 1
Real-World Operational Breakdown Observed
Engineering Solution Implemented in Capstone 2
No Sequential Multi-Stop Routing Formula
Paper stated ₱30 for extra stores up to 2 stops, but lacked any formula for measuring cumulative road distance across multiple stops.
Codified exact sequential formula: D_total = sum(dist(Sk, Sk+1)) + dist(Sn, C) with 2.0km base radius allowance and ₱10/km excess.
Unstated Database Authority & Source of Truth
Paper listed MySQL and Firebase in Figure 2, but never specified which database has authoritative truth during status conflicts.
Defined strict hybrid partition: MariaDB is the ACID source of truth for money, orders, and users; Firebase is a live projection for telemetry.
GPS Stationary Jitter & Signal Bouncing
Paper assumed phone GPS returns clean coordinates. Inside metal-roof commercial stores, GPS bounces 30-80m, triggering false arrival alerts.
Built GPS Quality Gate rejecting accuracy >50m, dampening stationary jitter (<0.5m/s and <15m), and rejecting out-of-order timestamps.
Store Queue Wait Times (Dwell Time) vs Travel Time
Paper omitted delivery ETA calculations. Driving in Tacurong takes 5-8 mins; 80% of customer wait time is the rider queuing in stores.
Built background learning job (jobs/dwellLearning.ts) tracking P50/P80 queue wait times per store category to render honest ETA windows.
Multi-Dispatcher Concurrent Order Collisions
Paper diagrams allowed dispatchers to assign riders, but lacked concurrency guards if two dispatchers click the same order simultaneously.
Engineered Single-Dispatcher Ownership Scoping (verifyDispatcherAccess) preventing BOLA/IDOR conflicts with dedicated conflict UI.
Arbitrary Barangay Zones vs Actual Road Geography
Paper proposed ₱70 Poblacion + ₱10 neighboring barangay zones. A store 200m away across a border was unfairly surcharged vs 3.5km in-zone.
Retired the Zone model completely. Integrated Open Source Routing Machine (OSRM) and Google Directions for road-network distance.
Commercial SMS Gateway Cost Barrier
Paper promised automated SMS for OTPs and status alerts. Commercial SMS gateways cost ₱0.50-₱1.00/SMS, creating unsustainable recurring costs.
Implemented secure Universal SMTP Email OTP Relay via Nodemailer and Expo Push Notifications, operating with 100% free delivery.
Enterprise Security, Token Lifespans & Rate Limiting
Security requirements only had 3 sentences. Lacked password hashing specs, session hijacking defenses, or brute-force rate limiting.
Implemented Bcrypt hashing, 15-min memory access tokens, 30-day rotating refresh tokens in user_sessions, and express-rate-limit.
Manual Rider Typo Risk on Receipt Amounts
REQ023 only asked for a receipt photo, assuming riders accurately type numbers manually while rushing on the field.
Integrated Google ML Kit OCR text recognition (@react-native-ml-kit/text-recognition) to auto-extract printed receipt totals via camera.
Budget Phone Viewport Distortion (Samsung A04)
Paper assumed generic Android 10 screens. On real riders' phones (Samsung A04, 360dp width), fonts clipped and keyboards covered submit buttons.
Engineered mathematical typography clamping [0.85x, 1.10x], 60/120 FPS hardware transforms, and 110dp bottom scroll clearance.
Offline Action Duplication & Idempotency
Paper promised SQLite caching, but lacked rules for preventing duplicate errand updates when offline devices reconnect to the server.
Built idempotent action logging with unique clientPointId and backfilled timestamps, ensuring zero duplicate errand charges on reconnect.
